newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Goodman still pursuing Defiance NZ assets.
newsitem.headline: Goodman still pursuing Defiance NZ assets.

text.p: Food and bakery group Goodman Fielder said on Friday it was continuing discussions with the New Zealand Commerce Commission (NZCC) regarding the acquisition of the New Zealand assets of Defiance Mills Ltd.

On April 14. the NZCC said it would not clear the original planned NZ$48 million purchase, saying that it was not satisfied that, should the acquisition go ahead, Goodman would not acquire or strengthen a dominant position in a number of markets.
Goodman said the company planned to lodge a revised application with the Commerce Commission and was working with Defiance Foods to develop a revised proposal.
However, a High Court appeal against the April decision, to be filed on Friday would preserve the company's position on the original application.

"We remain committed to the acquisition of Defiance Foods milling and baking operations in New Zealand and are keeping all options open, including a new NZCC application and a High Court appeal," said Goodman chief executive officer David Hearne.
Hearn said Goodman was examining the possibility of divesting some New Zealand assets to meet NZCC concerns.
"But this option will only be pursued if it makes good commercial sense," he said.
By 12.45 p.m. (0245 GMT), Goodman shares were a cent lower at A$1.64 on turnover of 1.1 million shares, while Defiance shares were untraded but bid five cents lower at A$1.95.
